events.what: Hegde, Sandeep and Shashank prove the conjecture for P13-free graphs
Carr proves graphs of diameter 2 and minimum degree at least 3 contain a cycle of length 4 or 8
Exhaustive certified search shows no cubic bipartite counterexample on fewer than 60 vertices
events.ai_basis: OpenAI ChatGPT materially assisted the initial research, including developing computational and structural approaches, portions of the incidence-based code and preliminary arguments

events.what: SAT search with DRAT certificates shows no minimum-degree-3 counterexample on fewer than 24 vertices
events.ai_basis: Computations were carried out with the assistance of an AI system (Claude)

judgement.doubts: Agree with the 2026-09-28 hand corrections. Minimal-counterexample order results check every graph up to n vertices and are instances (F4), so their AI disclosures do not set ai_role. Carr's paper is recorded as published (2026-01-30), so it may count as digested; both surviving events are human cases of the same tier with no AI, so the codes are the same either way. The bullet says 'cubic graphs' while the conjecture is usually stated for minimum degree 3; P13-free and diameter-2 are restrictions under either reading.
